title: When the small talk dies
situation: You're at your friend Nisha's housewarming, and she's the only person you know. By the snacks, you and a stranger swapped names and jobs. Now there's a silence.
goal: Turn this into a real conversation you'd both enjoy.

partner.name: Sam
partner.hiddenWant: Sam also only knows Nisha and would be relieved if someone kept talking, but won't carry the conversation alone.
softensWhen: You build on what they said
digsInWhen: You talk about yourself too long

rubric.name: Asked a real question
rubric.tip: Swap "what do you do" for "how did you end up doing it."

rubric.name: Offered something of yourself
rubric.tip: Give a small, honest detail. People match what you offer.

rubric.name: Built on what they said
rubric.tip: Pick one word from their last answer and ask about it.

rubric.name: Kept it light
rubric.tip: A little self-deprecating humour makes it easier for both of you.

partnerLine.neutral: Nice. So... yeah. This dip's good.
partnerLine.open: Nice. So... yeah. Honestly, this dip is the best thing here.

choices.text: It is. I've been standing near it on purpose, because I only know Nisha. How do you know her?
choices.reaction: Ha, same. Only Nisha. We worked together, like, two jobs ago.
choices.coachNote: Admitting you only know the host is honest, and it gives them an easy way in.

choices.text: Yeah. So what else do you do, apart from UX research?
choices.reaction: Uh, not much. Work, sleep. You?
choices.coachNote: It's a question, but another résumé question. It keeps things on the surface.
choices.betterLine: What's the strangest thing you've learned from watching people use apps?

choices.text: Did you see the match last night? Unreal ending.
choices.reaction: I, uh, don't really follow it. Sorry.
choices.coachNote: Jumping to something unrelated means Sam has to catch up or admit they can't.
choices.betterLine: I've been standing near it on purpose, because I only know Nisha. You?

partnerLine.guarded: Yeah. It's fine. The job's fine.
partnerLine.neutral: UX research is basically watching people get confused by apps.
partnerLine.open: My job is honestly just watching people get confused by apps and trying not to laugh.

choices.text: Wait, that sounds great. What's the most confused you've seen someone get?
choices.reaction: Oh, okay. There was this guy who tried to swipe a paper form. Genuinely.
choices.coachNote: You picked up their exact words and asked for a story, which is easier to answer than a fact.

trigger.label: You build on what they said

choices.text: Oh cool, I'm in product, so I work with researchers a lot. We did like twenty interviews on my last project, and it was really interesting because...
choices.coachNote: Relating is good, but you took the spotlight before they'd finished stepping into it.
choices.betterLine: Ha, I've done a few interviews myself. What's the most confused you've seen someone get?

trigger.label: You talk about yourself too long

choices.text: Haha, so you're basically professionally judging people?
choices.coachNote: Teasing a stranger's job before you know them can land as a jab, not a joke.
choices.betterLine: That sounds great. What's the most confused you've seen someone get?

partnerLine.neutral: Anyway. What about you? Why are you here if you only know Nisha?
partnerLine.open: Okay, your turn. Why are you here if you only know Nisha? Be honest.

choices.text: Honestly? I almost bailed. I'm glad I didn't, though. This beats my couch.
choices.reaction: Ha. I almost bailed too. Twice.
choices.coachNote: A small, honest admission invites them to match it, and they did.

choices.text: Just being supportive, you know. Nisha's a good friend.
choices.coachNote: True, but safe. It closes the topic instead of opening one.
choices.betterLine: Honestly? I almost bailed. I'm glad I didn't.

choices.text: Parties aren't really my thing. Most of these people seem kind of boring.
choices.reaction: Oh. Well, I'm one of these people, I guess.
choices.coachNote: Honesty is good, but calling the room boring includes the person you're talking to.
choices.betterLine: Honestly? I almost bailed. This beats my couch, though.

partnerLine.guarded: Yeah. Well. I'm gonna grab a refill.
partnerLine.neutral: Okay, this is nice. I'm gonna grab a refill, though. Want anything?
partnerLine.open: Okay, this is the first real conversation I've had tonight. I'm grabbing a refill. Want one?

choices.text: Yes, please. And then you owe me the rest of the paper-form story.
choices.reaction: Deal. It gets worse, I promise.
choices.coachNote: A callback shows you were really listening, and gives them a reason to come back.

trigger.label: You build on what they said

choices.coachNote: Polite, but it lets the conversation end right as it was warming up.
choices.betterLine: Yes, please. And you owe me the rest of that story.

choices.text: Sure. Hey, can I get your number, just in case?
choices.reaction: Oh. Um, I'm on Instagram, I guess?
choices.coachNote: Asking for a number mid-refill skips a few steps. Let the conversation finish first.
choices.betterLine: Yes, please. And then you owe me the rest of that story.

endings.guarded: Nice meeting you. Enjoy the party.
endings.neutral: Nice talking to you. Find me if you need rescuing from small talk.
endings.open: Okay, you're sitting with me when Nisha makes everyone play games. That's the rule.
